title: $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$ is flat over $E_X$
statement:
For a finite extension $E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Qlb$ and every scheme $X$, the extension
of scalars $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}\otimes_{E_X}-\colon\Mod_{E_X}\to\Mod_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}}$ along
$E_X\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$ ([def-sfb-subfield-to-qlbar-coefficient-map],
[sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]) preserves finite limits; that is, $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$ is flat over
$E_X$.

proof.text: Put $R=E_X$ and $B=\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$. Work on the small pro-étale site of $X$, in a coefficient universe containing its skeleton and the set of finite subextensions. The internal modules of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] identify with the sheaves of modules of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]: by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], a map $R\otimes M\to M$ is a compatible family of bilinear sectionwise actions, and its unit and associativity equations are precisely the ordinary module laws. This identifies morphisms too. Under this identification the coequalizer in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] is the relative sheaf tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]: maps out of either are exactly compatible bilinear maps satisfying $(sr,m)\mapsto(s,rm)$. Thus all later assertions about sheaves of modules apply to the internal modules and to the very extension-of-scalars functor in the statement.

source.place: first sentence and tensor sentence: identification of the module and tensor conventions

proof.text: Let $I$ be the set of finite subextensions $F\subseteq\Qlb$ containing $E$, ordered by inclusion. It contains $E$ and is directed: the compositum of two such fields is a finite common upper bound by [det-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed-subextensions]. The ring colimit in [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] may be restricted to $I$. Explicitly, a cocone on $I$ extends to all finite subextensions by assigning to $H$ the composite $H_X\to(EH)_X\to T$. For $H\subseteq H'$ the square commutes after passing to $EH'$, and for $H\supseteq E$ the extension is the original map. Conversely any cocone on all subextensions is forced to have this extension by its compatibility with $H\subseteq EH$. Thus the cocone universal properties agree. Its vertex is $B$, and [lem-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map-comp] says its legs are $R$-linear for the $R$-actions induced by $E_X\to F_X$ and the specified $E_X\to B$.

source.place: first sentence: restricting the coefficient colimit to F containing E

proof.text: Here the coefficient colimit also holds in $R$-modules; the following argument avoids assuming that a colimit in rings is automatically a module colimit. Form $C=\operatorname{colim}_{F\in I}F_X$ in $R$-modules, with maps $j_F$, using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. By [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits], tensoring on the left by any fixed $R$-module preserves this colimit. The balanced maps $x\otimes y\mapsto y\otimes x$ and $y\otimes x\mapsto x\otimes y$ are inverse $R$-linear maps by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], since $R$ is commutative; they commute with morphisms on each factor. Thus tensoring on the right by a fixed module also preserves this colimit. Define multiplication on $C$ as follows: for $F,G\in I$ choose a common upper field $H$ and use $F_X\otimes_R G_X\to H_X\xrightarrow{j_H}C$, where the first map is multiplication after inclusion. A larger upper field gives the same map, and any two choices have a common upper field, so these maps are independent of the choice and compatible in both variables. Applying the tensor-colimit universal property twice gives $C\otimes_R C\to C$. The map $R=E_X\xrightarrow{j_E}C$ is its unit. Associativity, commutativity and the unit equations follow by precomposing with three, two or one of the maps $j_F$, respectively, and placing the finitely many fields in a single upper field; the tensor-colimit property makes these tests determine the maps. For any compatible ring cocone $F_X\to T$, give $T$ its $R$-action from its $E$-leg. The unique $R$-linear map $C\to T$ preserves multiplication because on each $F_X\otimes_R G_X$, after passage to an upper field $H$, the two maps are the ring-cocone map $H_X\to T$ applied to the product of the two included factors; these maps agree as that cocone map is multiplicative. It preserves the unit because its composite with $j_E:R\to C$ is the given unit-preserving map $R\to T$. Thus $C$ is the ring colimit of the restricted diagram. The preceding step identifies its canonical map $C\to B$ as an isomorphism of rings under $R$, hence also of $R$-modules. Consequently $B\cong\operatorname{colim}_{I}F_X$ as $R$-modules, with the specified inclusions.

source.place: Tags 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits) and 03EP (lemma-tensor-commute-colimits), applied twice to construct multiplication on the module colimit

proof.text:
Write $T(M)$ for the underlying $R$-module of $B\otimes_R M$, and $T_F(M)$ for the underlying $R$-module of $F_X\otimes_R M$. The preceding module-colimit identification and [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits] give a natural isomorphism
$$\theta_M:\operatorname{colim}_{F\in I}T_F(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(M).$$
Its component on the $F$-leg sends $s\otimes m$ to $\iota_F(s)\otimes m$. The transition $T_F(M)\to T_G(M)$ is $s\otimes m\mapsto\iota_{FG}(s)\otimes m$, and a morphism $u:M\to N$ sends $s\otimes m$ to $s\otimes u(m)$; these formulas commute, proving the claimed naturality. These are maps of the sheafified relative tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The colimit here is in $R$-modules. Individual terms are not asserted to be $B$-modules.

source.place: Tag 03EP (lemma-tensor-commute-colimits), item (2); canonical comparison and its naturality

proof.text: For every $F\in I$, [lem-sfb-subfield-flat] gives preservation of finite limits by extension $F_X\otimes_R-$. Restriction from $F_X$-modules to $R$-modules preserves limits by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], so $T_F$ preserves finite limits. In particular, for any $R$-linear morphism $u:M\to N$ with kernel $K$, the natural morphism $T_F(K)\to T_F(M)$ identifies $T_F(K)$ with $\ker(T_F(u))$. The transitions from the preceding step commute with these kernel maps. All of these assertions are in a fixed category of $R$-modules, although the finite extensions initially take values in different categories of $F_X$-modules.

source.place: last sentence: finite-stage flatness, after restricting all stages to E_X

proof.text:
Filtered colimits in $R$-modules preserve these kernels. To verify the exactness needed here using precisely the statements cited, set $A_F=T_F(K)$, $D_F=T_F(M)$, $H_F=T_F(N)$, $J_F=\operatorname{im}(T_F(u))$ and $Q_F=\operatorname{coker}(T_F(u))$. Commutativity with transitions induces diagrams $J_F$ and $Q_F$, with short exact sequences
$$0\to A_F\to D_F\to J_F\to0,\qquad0\to J_F\to H_F\to Q_F\to0.$$
By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], forgetting the $R$-actions preserves these sequences and all their colimits. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact] to both underlying diagrams. The resulting inclusion $\operatorname{colim}J_F\to\operatorname{colim}H_F$ is monic, so the kernel of $\operatorname{colim}D_F\to\operatorname{colim}H_F$ is $\operatorname{colim}A_F$. This is also the kernel in $R$-modules: the forgetful functor computes limits, and the unique factorization through the underlying kernel is $R$-linear (apply its monic inclusion to the scalar-linearity equation). With the natural isomorphisms $\theta_K,\theta_M,\theta_N$ of the preceding steps, this proves $T(K)\cong\ker(T(u))$.

The functor $T$ is additive and preserves zero and finite products. Indeed $B\otimes_R0=0$, and the mutually inverse maps
$$B\otimes_R(M\oplus N)\longrightarrow(B\otimes_R M)\oplus(B\otimes_R N),\quad b\otimes(m,n)\longmapsto(b\otimes m,b\otimes n),$$
$$ (b\otimes m,0)\longmapsto b\otimes(m,0),\qquad(0,b\otimes n)\longmapsto b\otimes(0,n)$$
are balanced bilinear formulas, hence induce sheaf morphisms by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; the composites are identities by additivity of tensor. The same formula $b\otimes(u+v)(m)=b\otimes u(m)+b\otimes v(m)$ proves additivity on morphisms. Products and kernels are computed sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise], so finite direct sums are also finite products. For a finite diagram $D:J\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$, its limit is the kernel of
$$\prod_{j\in\operatorname{Ob}J}D_j\longrightarrow\prod_{a:j\to k\in\operatorname{Mor}J}D_k,\qquad(x_j)_j\longmapsto(D(a)x_j-x_k)_a.$$
This formula follows directly from the compatible-family description in that same node. Apply product preservation, additivity and the kernel preservation already proved: the kernel is taken to the identical compatible-family kernel for $T\circ D$. Therefore $T$ preserves every finite limit, including the empty limit $0$.

source.place: Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), limits paragraph, plus the explicit balanced tensor formulas and the finite-diagram kernel formula

proof.text:
Let $\operatorname{Ext}(M)=B\otimes_R M$ with its $B$-action. For a finite diagram $D$ the canonical map
$$a:\operatorname{Ext}(\lim D)\longrightarrow\lim(\operatorname{Ext}\circ D)$$
is $B$-linear. Limits of $B$-modules and of $R$-modules are computed sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise], so restriction takes the right-hand limit to the $R$-module limit of $T\circ D$. The preceding step says the underlying $R$-linear map of $a$ is invertible. Its inverse is $B$-linear: for a local scalar $b$ and section $y$, apply the injective map $a$ to get $a(b\,a^{-1}(y))=b\,y=a(a^{-1}(b\,y))$. Thus $a$ is an isomorphism of $B$-modules. This proves preservation of finite limits for the extension along the coefficient map in the statement.
